steps.what: Clarify the actual music-project, commercial or film-postproduction brief, cue timing, intended instruments and required MIDI delivery format with the production team.
inputs: Actual production brief and picture or musical reference
outputs: Actual cue scope, timing and delivery constraints

steps.what: Choose the actual MIDI instrument assignments, channel/routing map, tempo basis and required controls in the digital audio workstation {OTHER} for this production.
inputs: Actual cue and delivery constraints from s1
Actual available instruments and device mappings
outputs: Technician-authored actual instrument/routing and timing choices

steps.what: Set up the actual repeated MIDI tracks, channel assignments and routing fields from the selected map using native workstation track templates {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual selected instrument/routing map from s2
outputs: Draft configured MIDI session tracks with the selected routing

steps.what: Create the actual musical instrument digital interface program by performing or entering notes, velocities, articulations and controller events in the workstation {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual configured draft tracks from s3
Actual musical brief and technician's creative choices
outputs: Actual authored MIDI events and musical program draft

steps.what: Edit the actual MIDI program's timing, expression and instrument balance against the music or picture cue, listening and correcting in the workstation {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual music or picture reference and delivery constraints
outputs: Complete actual edited MIDI session draft

steps.what: Produce the actual delivery-format MIDI file draft from the complete edited workstation session {OTHER} with its native export.
inputs: Complete actual edited session from s5

steps.what: Check and correct the complete actual session and exported MIDI file by playback/reimport, checking cue synchronisation, note/control events, instrument mappings and the exact intended production recipient.
inputs: Actual exported delivery draft from s6
Actual brief, mappings and delivery requirements
outputs: Exact checked final MIDI program/session and delivery file, with recipient

steps.what: Save the exact checked final MIDI session and delivery file in the production workspace {OTHER}.
inputs: Exact completed session and delivery file checked in s7
outputs: Saved final MIDI program and delivery file

steps.what: Send the exact checked final MIDI delivery file to the designated external production client through {EMAIL}.
inputs: Unchanged final MIDI file saved in s8

tasks.design: Configure native workstation track templates for the actual selected MIDI routing. Retain instrument choices, actual musical-event creation, expression editing and playback checks. Export the real draft before checking it, then separately save and deliver the checked file.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual repeated manual track/channel/routing setup around creative MIDI programming.
tasks.enabler_now: Native workstation track templates populated from the technician's selected map.
tasks.still_hard: Musical expression, picture timing and device-specific playback interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Hear whether the actual program serves the production rather than merely containing valid MIDI events.

ambition.what: No automatic composition, instrument choice or public release.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated session setup, unchanged creative authorship and sound checking.

reach.learn: Check actual exported playback and mapping rather than the session alone

evidence.claim: Native audio-workstation templates can repeat track and routing configuration without composing the actual MIDI performance.

assumptions: Shares are conditional E1 active-work estimates, not measured production baselines. Actual MIDI program creation, event editing, delivery-file production and handoff are included. No generic music-program generation or synthetic performance is substituted for the technician's work.

The production team supplies the actual brief and delivery constraints in s1 through unchanged work. The technician chooses the actual routing/timing map in s2 before s3 uses it and authors real MIDI events in s4. Missing device maps or untested templates require manual configuration; no free stable mapping is assumed.

Native templates come first; s3 replaces actual remaining repeated manual setup only. Already automatic track setup and rendering/export runtime give zero new saving. Template creation and mapping tests are included in build/upkeep. No saving on creative decisions, performance, editing or playback checks.

The actual export exists in s6 before the completed-version check s7. Corrections require regenerating the export and repeating final playback checks before saving or delivery. Ordinary final checking supplies requested save/send gates without additional self-approval labour. Both 1% save and 1% send remain fully retained with no saving. If the actual client is internal, use internal authority for the delivery branch.
research_questions: Does template setup reproduce the selected channel/routing map and does the actual exported file play correctly on the intended production setup?

already_counted.description: Actual briefing, creative mapping, MIDI-event authorship, editing, real export, playback checking, save and delivery remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain and test actual track templates and device mappings.

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed session and actual exported MIDI file checked in s7
Unchanged actual MIDI delivery file and client recipient checked in s7

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 15 actual repeated setup gross less 1 template/mapping upkeep gives 14. Zero if the setup is already native runtime; no gain on export, save or send.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less repeated MIDI session setup while musical programming and actual-file validation remain direct creative work.
role.ambitious_version: A sound technician who reuses tested setup accurately and retains authorship and responsibility for the actual program heard by the production.
